concepts.name: Scaled dot-product attention
concepts.summary: The atomic operation of attention: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) . V. Score every query against every key by dot product, scale by sqrt(d_k), soften to a probability distribution with softmax, then return the weighted blend of values. Score, scale, soften, blend.

concepts.name: Dot-product similarity
concepts.summary: Attention's measure of alignment: the dot product of a query and a key. For q=[1,0,2,1], the key [0,0,1,1] scores 3 while [1,1,0,0] scores 1, so the query leans toward the former. A larger dot product means greater likeness.

concepts.name: Softmax (normalise + sharpen)
concepts.summary: Softmax turns raw scores into attention weights, doing two jobs at once: it exponentiates (always positive, amplifying gaps so the winner wins by more) and normalises (weights sum to one). 'Normalise + sharpen': equal scores give near-uniform attention, large gaps give near one-hot. Preceded by scaling by sqrt(d_k) to keep gradients alive.

concepts.name: Q, K, V projections
concepts.summary: Q, K and V are three learned linear projections of the same input X (shape n x d_model): Q=X.Wq, K=X.Wk, V=X.Wv. The model learns what to ask, what to advertise, and what to give. Constraint: d_q = d_k always (the dot product demands it); d_v may differ.

concepts.name: The (n,n) score matrix — O(n²)
concepts.summary: The score matrix Q.K^T has shape (n, n) — every token's score to every token — making self-attention O(n^2) in sequence length. This (n,n) object is what later gets masked, cached, and (in Flash attention) never materialised.
